subject: Dedicated capacity: capacity-safety & spike-response proposal for VentureAI
messages:
From: Lily Zhang <lily@ventureai.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — spike handling and contractual guardrails

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. As we move toward a Dedicated commitment, procurement asked for a short, written summary of how Redwood handles short-term traffic spikes on Dedicated pools — specifically:

- how burst/shoulder capacity is applied vs. reserved slabs
- eviction and preemption order (what gets throttled first)
- typical headroom multipliers you recommend for ML inference workloads with diurnal spikes
- any credits or remediation if we experience throttling during a launch window

We’re aiming to finalize SLO language this week so any concise examples / numbers you can share would be great. I attached our traffic forecast export for reference.

Cheers,
Lily
Lily Zhang
Head of Platform, VentureAI
Attachment: ventureai_mrp_estimates.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lily Zhang <lily@ventureai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — spike handling and contractual guardrails

Hi Lily — thanks for the clear list. I’ll put together a short policy draft and numbers; copying Marcus for sizing + Karthik for ops knobs.

High level preview: we do a two-layer approach for Dedicated customers — reserved slab + transient shoulder pool. Typical guidance: 20–40% shoulder headroom for customers with predictable diurnal spikes; for launch events we recommend a temporary "event uplift" (2–4x on request) with a short notice window. Eviction order favors opportunistic/ephemeral workloads first; production pinned pools are last to be preempted.

I’ll send a formal proposal by EOD tomorrow and attach the short policy PDF for legal/procurement review.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: RE: internal - sizing notes for VentureAI (VT-4821)

Naomi / Karthik — quick notes based on the attached MRP:

- Baseline commitment: 120 A100-equivalent slots across two regions (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 failover).
- Typical 95th-pct req/sec during business hours: ~18k; launch day peaks in forecast show short bursts to ~62k for ~2 hours.
- Recommend slab that covers 95th pct steady-state (roughly 100 slots) + a shoulder pool of 30 slots (30% headroom). For the 62k launch spike, propose a time-bound event uplift: additional ephemeral 120 slots for up to 4 hours with the following guardrails:
  - Uplift request needs 24h notice for guaranteed allocation; we can support <24h best-effort but not guaranteed.
  - Uplift billing runs at a premium (1.6x) and includes a 1-hour cooldown grace credit if preemption occurs during the uplift window.
- Eviction: preemptible tasks (batch/queryless clients) -> ephemeral shoulder -> dedicated pinned production instances. If cluster pressure persists, we throttle low-priority real-time models first.

Attachments: I sketched a compact policy PDF (dedicated-spike-policy-draft.pdf) and numbers in the MRP. Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lily Zhang <lily@ventureai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-11-04T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: VentureAI spike-response proposal (attached)

Lily — attaching a compact proposal for your procurement and infra teams. Key points summarized below for easy redlining:

1) Baseline & shoulder: Reserved slab to cover steady-state 95th percentile (approx. 100 GPU slots) + shoulder pool of 30 slots (30% headroom) for short live spikes.
2) Event Uplift: For predictable launches, VentureAI can request temporary uplift (up to +120 slots for up to 4 hours). Guaranteed with 24h notice; best-effort <24h. Uplift billing at 1.6x.
3) Eviction & throttling order: preemptible batch workloads -> ephemeral shoulder -> pinned production. In extreme pressure, we apply prioritized token-level throttling on low-priority routes first.
4) Credits & remediation: If Redwood preempts guaranteed capacity during a confirmed uplift window (i.e., we fail to deliver guaranteed uplift), VentureAI will receive a service credit equal to the uplift fee for the first hour and an additional pro-rated credit for any subsequent period where the uplift SLA is not met.

Attached: dedicated-spike-policy-draft.pdf; summary spreadsheet included earlier. If this looks good I can provide a redline-friendly DOCX / HubSpot link for procurement.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with your procurement and infra to walk through specifics.

Best,
Naomi
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: dedicated-spike-policy-draft.pdf (pdf)
Related: HubSpot:HS-581234

From: Lily Zhang <lily@ventureai.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@ventureai.com>
Date: 2027-11-05T16:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: VentureAI spike-response proposal (attached)

Naomi / team — this is exactly what procurement needed, thank you. A couple quick points from procurement:

- They want the uplift-notice window captured in the contract (24h guaranteed / best-effort shorter).
- A request for a clearer definition of "preemptible batch" in the eviction order (suggested: jobs launched via the batch API with priority flag = low).
- Procurement asked if the 1-hour grace credit can be extended to 2 hours for launch windows only — they will trade some additional uplift spend for that protection.

Operationally, infra wants a small onboarding pilot next month (2 weeks) to validate the shoulder behavior at production scale. Can Redwood provision a trial shoulder pool corresponding to 20% headroom for ~14 days? If yes, we can run the pilot in early December and move forward with the contract redline in parallel.

Let me know the internal owner on your side for the pilot and procurement negotiations and we’ll loop Legal.

Thanks,
Lily
Head of Platform, VentureAI
